quarterly_data.signal: Eversource's Q2 2026 earnings slides (Exhibit 99.3) show the 2026-2030 capital investment plan ($26.5 billion, focused on load growth and reliability, excluding Aquarion after its sale) as a $2.3 billion increase compared to the prior five-year forecast, and list potential incremental investments during and beyond the forecast period of $1.7 billion: $1 Billion for Connecticut AMI and $700 Million for the ISO-NE Longer-Term Transmission Planning RFP. The slides describe the ISO-NE preliminary preferred Avangrid/Eversource solution as using existing rights of way with a 2.2x benefit/cost ratio.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026-2030 plan +$2.3 billion vs prior five-year forecast; potential incremental investments $1.7 billion ($1 Billion CT AMI, $700 Million LTTP RFP); LTTP preferred solution 2.2x benefit/cost
